issue_summary: The deployed average endpoint accepts a zero divisor and serializes the non-finite result as null.

diagnosis.summary: The calculate-average route divides by count without validating that it is finite and non-zero, so a zero divisor returns HTTP 200 with a null JSON value instead of a typed client error.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: GET /calculate-average/10/0 returned HTTP 200 with {"average":null}; division by zero is not rejected.

acceptance_criteria: A zero divisor returns HTTP 400 with a typed JSON error instead of HTTP 200 with a null average.
Finite non-zero inputs preserve correct numeric division, including 10 divided by 2 returning 5.
Average calculation is extracted to dependency-free logic in lib/calculate-average.js.
tests/calculate-average.test.js uses the built-in node:test runner to cover zero and non-zero divisors.
No dependency manifest, lock file, deployment workflow, or production environment is changed.
